bottom_line: During the treatment period, stroke or systemic embolic event occurred at 1.18% per year with high-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio vs. warfarin, 0.79; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 0.63 to 0.99).
implications: In this trial, during the treatment period, high-dose edoxaban had a lower annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolic event than warfarin (1.18% vs 1.50% per year; hazard ratio, 0.79; 97.5% CI, 0.63 to 0.99), while low-dose edoxaban had a similar rate to warfarin (1.61% vs 1.50% per year; hazard ratio, 1.07; 97.5% CI, 0.87 to 1.31). Both edoxaban regimens had lower annualized major bleeding than warfarin (2.75% and 1.61% vs 3.43% per year). These numbers support conclusions about comparative efficacy and bleeding rates as defined and adjudicated in this study, and do not by themselves establish effects outside the study population or beyond the trial’s defined treatment/analysis periods.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, three-group trial comparing two once-daily edoxaban regimens vs warfarin.
major_points.quote: The Effective Anticoagulation with Factor Xa Next Generation in Atrial Fibrillation–Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 48 (ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48) trial was a three-group, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial comparing two dose regimens of edoxaban with warfarin.

major_points.text: Enrolled 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation; median follow-up 2.8 years.
